description: Studies Silko’s Ceremony through braided oral and written storytelling, war memory, mixed ancestry, land dispossession, and the adaptation of healing practices. Connects the Pacific War with uranium extraction in New Mexico, examining Tayo’s refusal to repeat violence and the role of community in making his experience tellable.
